independence. A dash means the formulation has no such parameter. Coverage and

extrapolation.

## Dewaele (2019), Pb MAO-scale Vinet

`lead_hcp_dewaele_2019_mao_vinet` · Executable

- **Printed parameter errors:** 95% half-widths (1.96 sigma)

Vinet fit to static diamond-anvil-cell X-ray compression data in helium or neon, reduced with the Mao-1986 ruby scale. The fit also includes earlier Kuznetsov et al. hcp data on the Brown NaCl scale; the paper does not state the subset, weights or scale treatment used. The Dorogokupets-2007-scale record is an alternative reduction of the same data, not an independent experiment.

## Kuznetsov et al. (2002), 296 K hcp BM3 slice

`lead_hcp_kuznetsov_2002_bm3_3` · Executable

Reproduction: **untested** · [Reconstruction report](../reconstruction-reports/lead_hcp.md#record-lead_hcp_kuznetsov_2002_bm3_3)

**Source check:** Coefficients from the hcp entries of Table 2 at T0 = 296 K (Equations 1-3); the printed V0 = 29.908 Å³/atom is stored per two-atom hcp cell.

    - **Year:** 2002
    - **Title:** FCC-HCP phase boundary in lead
    - **Source:** Solid State Communications
    - **Volume:** 122

- **Validity:**
    - **Pressure gpa:** \[12.0, 40.0\]
    - **Temperature k:** \[296.0, 296.0\]
    - **Notes:** 296 K slice of a P-V-T model fitted to experiments extending to 40 GPa and 800 K.; At room temperature transformation begins near 12 GPa and fcc-hcp coexistence persists to about 20 GPa; this is not a sharp equilibrium stability boundary.

Published 296 K isotherm of the source's temperature-dependent hcp BM3 model; the full P-V-T surface is outside the current thermal schema.

<details markdown="1">
<summary>Source review</summary>

- **Note:** Independently checked against the cited primary publication; no external software catalog was used as scientific authority.
- **Audit date:** 2026-09-08

    - **Access URL:** https://doi.org/10.1016/S0038-1098(02)00112-6
    - **DOI:** 10.1016/S0038-1098(02)00112-6
    - **Locations:** Equations 1-3; Tables 1-2; Figures 2-3
    - **Finding:** The stored BM3 record is exactly the 296 K isotherm of the published hcp P-V-T surface: V0=29.908 A^3/atom, B0=54.2 GPa, and B0\_prime=3.61.
- **Primary data check:**
    - **Status:** combined\_primary\_data\_partially\_bundled

    - **Source locations:** Table 1 and Figure 3
    - **Finding:** The slice reproduces seven digitized solid room-temperature hcp markers with 0.266 GPa pressure RMSE. All 21 direct and source-reduced markers give 0.642 GPa RMSE; the complete original P-V-T rows and fit protocol are unavailable.
    - **Reproduction resource:** docs/literature-reproductions/fortes-2019-fcc-pb.md

</details>
